business_problem: AGL needed to offer always-on digital support across web, account and mobile channels while reducing the load on frontline agents and enabling more transactions to be completed in self-service.
solution_summary: AGL evolved its customer-support assistant into a multichannel self-service platform built on IBM watsonx Assistant. The team replaced an earlier bot with a new assistant that answers FAQs, personalizes interactions through APIs and serves different content depending on whether the customer is on the public website, authenticated account portal or mobile app. Over time the implementation expanded from simple question answering into transactional journeys that can complete actions, not just route them. Those journeys are integrated with the company's ERP software, and newer flows include validating concession cards with the issuing body in real time and writing the result back to CRM without agent intervention. With IBM and systems integrator ISW, AGL also modernized the experience through Watson Actions. The result is a customer-service layer that combines conversational support, API orchestration and enterprise-system integration to automate routine service requests at scale.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx Assistant
solution_components.role: Powers the AGL Assistant across channels and executes both FAQ and transactional self-service journeys.

data_flow: Customer chats enter through AGL.com.au, My Account or the mobile app, watsonx Assistant calls APIs and ERP-connected workflows to personalize the interaction, and results such as validated concession-card updates are written back to CRM without agent handling.
business_outcome: AGL increased the share of customer interactions resolved in self-service, broadened the assistant from FAQs to transactions, and created a stronger 24x7 support option for millions of customers across multiple channels.
